subject: Availability: short outage impact on payment authorizations
messages:
From: Rob Hayes <rob@clarapay.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: payments+acct@clarapay.com
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Availability: short outage impact on payment authorizations

Hi Priya / Karthik,

We saw a ~7m window this morning (09:02–09:09 PST) where a subset of our authorization requests returned 503 / service-unavailable from Redwood's hosted region (us-west-2). This affected ~14% of attempts for one of our high-throughput checkout lanes. Our payments team is seeing retries but the customer impact is material (several abandoned checkouts).

Can you confirm: 1) the exact availability window as seen on your side; 2) whether this meets the SLA "remedy" thresholds (we're looking for guidance on pro-rata credit eligibility); and 3) what raw evidence (traces / server logs) you can provide so we can reconcile with our telemetry?

I've attached the subset of request ids from our side and a short symptom log (Attachment: rtraces_20290422.log, text, 2.1MB). We need a formal statement for our procurement and billing team to start a remedy request.

—Rob
Rob Hayes
Head of Payments, ClaraPay
rob@clarapay.com
(Attachment: rtraces_20290422.log, text/plain)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Availability: short outage impact on payment authorizations

Rob — thanks for the heads up and the logs. Sorry for the disruption this morning.

Karthik / Marcus: can you pull the serving logs and SLO windows for us (us-west-2) and confirm the observed client-facing 5xx window? Please include the SLO calculation (service uptime numerator/denominator) and the raw trace bundle. I'll track this on the ClaraPay account and coordinate the remedy request next steps.

Rob — we'll aim to get an initial confirmation and the candidate window within 4 business hours; if we confirm an SLA violation we'll follow Redwood's remedy playbook and provide the evidence bundle plus a proposed pro-rata calculation.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Rob Hayes <rob@clarapay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2029 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability: short outage impact on payment authorizations

On Mon, Apr 22, 2029 at 09:15 Rob Hayes <rob@clarapay.com> wrote:
> We saw a ~7m window this morning (09:02–09:09 PST) where a subset of our authorization requests returned 503 / service-unavailable from Redwood's hosted region (us-west-2).

Hi all — quick update from the infra side. We pulled the continuous serving metrics and request logs for us-west-2. Summary: there was a downstream dependency spike (third-party disk latency) that caused a transient degradation in our request-handling path. The client-facing status codes show an elevated 5xx rate between 09:01:58 and 09:09:34 PST — peak error rate ~18% across the affected shard.

SLO calc: for the day 2029-04-22, our 99.9% availability SLO denominator is total successful + failed requests per minute. Within the reported window we observe a 99.82% availability figure (per-minute aggregation) which crosses the SLA threshold for an exception remedial review. I've attached the SLO workbook we used (Attachment: slo_calc_spreadsheet.xlsx) and a raw trace bundle pointer.

Attachments included: slo_calc_spreadsheet.xlsx (XLSX, 420KB) — contains minute-level uptime slices and the automated remediation eligibility flag. raw trace bundle: stored in shared Drive link (see below).

Marcus Lin — I'm going to need a short written confirmation of the outage window from the ops on-call for ClaraPay's remedy submission. Marcus, can you add the postmortem timeline draft as well?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
(Attachment: slo_calc_spreadsheet.xlsx, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Rob Hayes <rob@clarapay.com>, payments+acct@clarapay.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Apr 2029 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability: short outage impact on payment authorizations

Rob / ClaraPay team — following up with the formal confirmation and next steps. Per our internal review (see attached SLO workbook), Redwood observed the client-facing error spike between 2029-04-22T09:01:58-07:00 and 2029-04-22T09:09:34-07:00 for requests routed to the affected shard in us-west-2. Karthik's SLO calc flags that the aggregated per-minute availability during that period falls below our 99.9% target, which triggers a remedy evaluation under section 4.2 of the Agreement.

What we'll provide within the next 48 hours:
- Raw trace bundle and serving logs (filtered to the request ids you provided) — Attachment: rtraces_20290422.log
- The per-minute SLO workbook exported as CSV and the calculation steps — Attachment: slo_calc_spreadsheet.xlsx
- Draft postmortem timeline and mitigation plan for your review — Attachment: postmortem_timeline_draft.md

Next steps for ClaraPay: please confirm whether you want Redwood to open a formal remedy case (we will then prepare the pro-rata calculation and route it through finance). If you want to proceed we'll need a signed confirmation from your procurement team (email OK) so we can start the credit evaluation and apply any eligible adjustment to the next invoice cycle.

Apologies again for the interruption — Marcus is pulling a short incident narrative and will add mitigation items to avoid recurrence.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
(Attachments: rtraces_20290422.log; slo_calc_spreadsheet.xlsx; postmortem_timeline_draft.md)
